title: What went in, what came back, and who was counting
label: The numbers
lede: Quibi never published a financial statement or a subscriber count. What exists is the amount it said it raised, the amount it reportedly gave back, and two competing sets of download numbers: the company’s own, and Sensor Tower’s estimates. Both are shown, labelled.

blocks.title: Where $1.75 billion went
blocks.subtitle: Money raised in two rounds, and the part that reportedly went back to investors when the company closed. $ millions.

from.label: raised: $1.0B in August 2018 and $750M in March 2020

to.label: Not returned (derived remainder)
to.note: $1,750M less the $350M reportedly returned. It covers content, marketing, technology, staff and the cost of winding down. Quibi published no breakdown and we have not itemised it.

to.label: Returned to investors (reported)
to.note: Variety: Quibi “reportedly told investors that it would return $350 million of its cash on hand.” Deadline: “around $350 million still in the bank.”[^2][^16]

blocks.source: Amounts raised as stated by the company to Variety[^3]. The returned amount is press-reported, not confirmed by the company[^2][^16]. The remainder is derived and takes no account of what Roku paid for the shows, which was not disclosed[^16].

items.text: from launch on April 6, 2020 to the wind-down announcement on October 21 (derived).[^10]

not returned per day of service: $1.4B ÷ 239 days (derived from reported figures).[^3][^16]

blocks.title: The subscriber plan, and what was measured
blocks.subtitle: Millions of paying subscribers. Only the first bar is the company’s own number, and it comes from a press report.

items.label: First 910,000 sign-ups still paying after the trial (estimate)
items.note: Sensor Tower estimate, disputed by Quibi.[^9]

blocks.source: Target and projection from the Wall Street Journal’s report of June 14, 2020, as summarised by Tubefilter and Señal News[^7][^8]. Conversion estimate from Sensor Tower via The Verge[^9]. The actual number of paying subscribers was never published and is unknown.

blocks.title: Two counts of the same downloads
blocks.subtitle: Cumulative app downloads, millions. Sensor Tower’s estimates against the totals Quibi gave to the press on or near the same dates.
blocks.source: Sensor Tower estimates: 2.9M[^5], 3.8M[^7], 4.5M[^9], 9.6M[^12]. Company figures: 1.7M[^6], 3.5M[^5], 5M[^7], “over 5.6 million”[^9]. Quibi gave no total in October and Sensor Tower’s week-one total was not in our sources. Downloads are not subscribers.

blocks.title: The launch spike, and what followed
blocks.subtitle: Average app installs per day, thousands, between the dates of successive Sensor Tower estimates. Derived from estimates; read it as a shape, not a measurement.

series.label: Average installs per day (derived from Sensor Tower estimates)

points.title: April 6: 379,000 in a day
points.text: Sensor Tower’s estimate for launch day, the peak. The app reached No. 3 in Apple’s App Store.[^4][^7]

points.title: The 90-day trial does not hold the pace
points.text: By May 11 the estimated total was 2.9 million. Katzenberg blamed the pandemic.[^5]

points.title: Under 25,000 a day
points.text: The Journal reported fewer than 20,000 a day in the first week of June. Free trials began expiring in early July.[^7][^9]

points.title: A late rise that did not matter
points.text: Sensor Tower put the total at about 9.6 million by October 21, but first-time installs in October were down 41% on September, and the company closed.[^12]

blocks.source: Sensor Tower estimates as reported by the New York Times[^5], the Wall Street Journal via Tubefilter[^7], The Verge[^9] and The Hollywood Reporter[^12]. Daily averages are derived: the change between two cumulative estimates divided by the days between them (arithmetic in the data notes).

blocks.body: Quibi’s reported first-year plan, from the New York Times: seven million users, $250 million in subscriber revenue and $470 million of marketing.[^5] The Journal’s figure for the subscriber target is 7.4 million.[^8] We use the Journal’s number in the charts and note the difference here.
